text.p: Technology Cost Optimisation — Diagnostic Findings and Delivery Roadmap
Meridian Retail Group · Steering Committee · June 2026

slide.text: Executive summary: a £33m run-rate saving is achievable by FY28

text.p: Meridian's technology spend has grown 2.3x faster than revenue since FY22, reaching £142m — 4.1% of revenue against a retail peer median of 2.9%.
Four structural drivers account for 78% of the gap: legacy ERP run costs, duplicated cloud estates, vendor sprawl, and manual service operations.
A three-wave programme can remove £33m of annual run-rate by FY28, with £9m landing in the first 12 months at low delivery risk.
The first wave is self-funding: contract renegotiations and cloud rightsizing require no capital investment and begin returning cash in Q2.

stack.text: Two-thirds of spend keeps the lights on
Run-and-maintain plus licences consume 56% of the budget before any change is delivered. Peer retailers hold this below 45%.
The change portfolio itself is healthy in size but fragmented: 61 initiatives across 9 steering groups, with no single value gate.
Implication: the saving is not "spend less on change" — it is "stop paying premium prices to stand still."

The bridge from £142m to a £109m run-rate
A classic long tail: four driver categories explain most of the addressable cost
Vendor strategy: five contracts carry the first wave
Savings are annualised run-rate at steady state; one-off renegotiation costs are absorbed in existing budgets.
Delivery roadmap: three waves over twelve months
What could knock the programme off course

text.p: Key risks
Northgate renewal slips past Q3, deferring the largest single saving
Cloud rightsizing degrades peak-trading performance
Service-desk automation triggers union consultation delays
Change fatigue: 61 in-flight initiatives compete for the same engineers
Mitigations
Begin renewal negotiation in month 1 with a credible exit alternative
Freeze rightsizing changes across the November–January trading window
Early works-council engagement; redeploy, don't release, L1 staff
Value gate at the exec checkpoint: stop or merge the bottom-quartile initiatives
Approve Wave 1 (commercial + cloud) for immediate mobilisation — £12.1m annualised, no capital required.
Mandate the value gate: every in-flight initiative re-baselined against the Atlas business case by end of Q1.
Appoint a single accountable owner for the vendor estate with delegated negotiation authority.
Commit to the FY28 target of £109m in the FY27 budget letter, so savings are banked rather than reabsorbed.
